tag: Earnings season meets the macro calendar
title: When CPI and earnings land in the same session, who reads the 10-Q?
sub: Every US earnings 8-K since 2005, timed to the second, tested against the Fed, CPI and jobs calendar.
The Fed's eight meetings a year sit inside earnings season. One announcement in seven shares its first trading session with CPI, the jobs report or the FOMC statement.

tag: Announcements per day, 2005–2025 · orange dots are FOMC days
title: Two bands are earnings season. The Fed meets in the darker one.
The acceptance stamp separates the sessions
sub: A 06:46 filing on a CPI day competes with the 08:30 print. A 16:30 filing on Fed day competes with nothing.

title: How the test was built
steps: Every 8-K with Item 2.02 from EDGAR; time of day from the acceptance stamp.
Crowded: the news first trades in the same session as CPI, payrolls or the FOMC statement.
Surprise two ways: first-filed GAAP EPS against last year, and the two-day market reaction.
60-day drift against FF5 plus momentum; firm and quarter fixed effects; errors clustered by firm and day.
Thresholds committed first. 2016–2025 held out and run once.

title: Crowded-session earnings drift like any other
sub: After the two-day reaction, top minus bottom surprise decile, 26,531 extreme events, 2005–2025.

title: The development sample said less drift. The holdout said no.
sub: Blue: the primary test in each sample. Grey: by release type. What replicates is zero.

title: Random calendars give the same answer
sub: 30% of 1,000 random macro calendars produce a larger coefficient than the holdout did.

title: The drift exists. The calendar doesn't move it.
sub: Split by Corwin-Schultz spread. Drift is 3.6x larger in illiquid names; the crowded-session effect is flat in all three.

title: Bad quarters are not hidden behind the Fed
sub: Same share of weak quarters on crowded and quiet sessions in both samples (t −0.01 and 1.2).

title: Bad news delays the filing, not the date
sub: Within-firm, t 5.8 on 177,209 announcements. Friday after the close: 1.7% against 1.4%.

title: Post-earnings drift, year by year
sub: Strongest in 2007 and 2024, zero in 2020. The crowding test runs inside this.

title: Neither book is a trade
sub: Quiet-session events 1.2 bp a day (t 1.9, 237 names); crowded 0.6 bp (t 0.4, 50 names). Net of spreads both lose.

title: Read these before the headline
items: Prices are from Yahoo Finance. Delisted firms are mostly missing; their crowded share was 14.6% against 15.9% for survivors.
GAAP EPS against last year is not the consensus number analysts trade.
Holdout standard error 0.66 pp: effects under about 1.3 pp, top versus bottom decile, are not ruled out.
Slides marked exploratory were not pre-registered. 737 tickers with a daily move over 100% were dropped whole.

title: Attention is not the scarce thing on Fed day.
sub: My read: the market absorbs an earnings release on a CPI, jobs or FOMC session about as fully as on a quiet one. Firms do not use those sessions to bury weak quarters; what they delay is the paperwork. What would change it: a consensus-based surprise, or delisted-firm prices, showing a gap this data cannot see.
